Expand grouped population to single-year ages while preserving an open group

Source: R/age.R
expand_age_pop.Rd

expand_age_pop() converts any set of closed age groups to single-year estimates and keeps the final source group as an actual open age group. It never represents an open group as a fabricated sequence of high ages. Every effective source-group total is constrained to its input total exactly, and estimates are non-negative.

Usage

expand_age_pop(
  x,
  source_breaks = c(0, 1, seq(5, 85, 5)),
  method = "linear",
  reference = NULL,
  high_age = "keep",
  pclm_control = list()
)

Arguments

x

Numeric population totals. Its length must equal length(source_breaks); the last value is the open age group.

source_breaks

Integer lower bounds of the input age groups. The last bound starts the open group. The default is 0, 1–4, 5–9, ..., 85+.

method

Splitting method: "linear", "constant", "fmm", "natural", "monoh.fc", "reference", "sprague", or "pclm". The spline options are retained for compatibility and apply only to closed groups. "reference" uses an external single-age schedule. "sprague" requires regular closed five-year groups; the default 0 and 1–4 groups are automatically combined to 0–4. "pclm" requires ungroup.

reference

An external single-age schedule for method = "reference". Supply a named numeric vector (names are ages), or a data frame with age/x and population/pop/y columns. It must cover every closed age to be split. It should be independent of data evaluated in a blind validation.

high_age

A character method or list supplied to expand_open_age_pop(). The default, "keep", retains the source open group. Use a list with method = "reference", reference, and max_age only when an external high-age schedule is available.

pclm_control

A list passed to ungroup::pclm(control = ...).

Value

A data frame with x (age lower bound), y (population), age_end, open, source_group, lower, and upper. Closed rows have age_end == x; the final open row has age_end = Inf. PCLM uncertainty intervals are returned when supplied by ungroup; other methods report missing intervals. Attributes record the effective source_breaks, method, and uncertainty method.

References

Sprague, T. B. (1880). Explanation of a new formula for interpolation. Journal of the Institute of Actuaries, 22, 270–285.

Rizzi, S., Gampe, J., and Eilers, P. H. C. (2015). Efficient ungrouping of coarse histograms and age heaping in demographic data. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 24(3), 291–313.

Examples

population <- c(
  5053, 17743, 25541, 32509, 30530, 34806, 36846, 38691, 40056,
  39252, 37349, 30507, 26363, 21684, 15362, 11725, 7461, 3260, 915
)
expand_age_pop(population, method = "sprague")
